text.p: NEW YORK - After a record-setting week on Wall Street, when stocks got a big boost from news on the economy and the balanced budget deal, investors may turn to smaller stocks that have lagged behind the overall market.
Analysts said that last week's rally finally began to extend beyond the small group of big-name stocks that have driven the Dow Jones industrial average near record highs.
The search for value appears to be moving into new territory.
"A lot of investors feel that the only areas with reasonable value are small- and mid-cap issues and some cyclicals," said Michael Metz, chief investment strategist at Oppenheimer & Co.
"The reason is the full exploitation of those stocks which figure prominently in the indexes and the sense that it is a folly to chase them at these levels."

The stock market rounded out a strong week with the Dow jumping 94.72 points to 7,071.20 on Friday - within 14 points of its record 7,085.16 set on March 11. For the week, the Dow gained 332.33 points, a record.

The move in companies with smaller market capitalisation, so-called small- and mid-cap stocks that have languished during the market's long rally, was welcome since it would broaden the previously narrow rally, analysts said.

Through Friday, the Dow industrials were up 9.7 percent for the year but the Nasdaq composite index of high-technology and smaller stocks had gained just 1.1 percent while the Russell 2000 index of small stocks had fallen 2.4 percent.
The numbers include impressive gains by the two smaller-cap indexes on Friday. 4,455.6, rising 85.9 from last Friday.

FRANKFURT - German shares edge up to a higher close after a rangebound bourse session, dulled by the fact that many market participants are away after the May Day holiday, many dealers see mid-term trend positive, given firm dollar and barring major shocks on U.S. economy. The DAX index closed up 22.30 points at 3,460.37, up 86.27 on the week. In post-bourse trade the DAX index stood at 3,491.08.
Wall Street could get some further fuel from investor enthusiasm for a deal on a framework for a balanced budget by 2002, announced by President Clinton and the Republican-led Congress late Friday.

LONDON - Leading UK shares scaled new peaks, inspired by bullish Wall Street and shrugging off uncertainties created by the Labour Party's historic sweep to power. The benchmark index rose early on, defying initial expectations for big drop, and then gathered pace in the final hours of the session as Wall Street leapt. PARIS - French shares closed 0.6 percent higher after a lacklustre and mixed day, the market had started with gains after having been closed on Thursday, ignoring Wall Street's overnight fall. It cut its gains ahead of the publication of weaker-than-expected April U.S. jobs creation data, spiked up after the numbers but the rally ran quickly out of steam. The CAC-40 index closed up 0.60 percent or 15.84 points at 2,655.31, rising 119.05 from seven days ago.

ZURICH - Swiss shares posted their third record session in a row and for the first time ended above the important 4,900 point level in the blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI), the market took a positive view of a patch of U.S. economic data and this led to a further improvement in interest rate prospects. The Broad SPI index rose 32.82 points or 1.06 percent to end at 3,127.47, a rise of 102.85 on the week.

TOKYO - Tokyo stocks surged to close at a new high for 1997, lifted by institutional investors, mostly pension funds, seeking blue-chip issues. The 225-share Nikkei average rose 239.42 points or 1.24 percent to end at 19,514.75, rising 901.89 from last week.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong stocks ended higher for the third day in a row, with a rally in property and bank stocks keeping the Hang Seng Index well above 13,000 points, although momentum began to slow after a strong week. The Hang Seng ended 60.92 points or 0.47 percent higher at 13,081.70, up 435.94 on the week.

SYDNEY - A resilient Australian share market locked in light single figure gains by the close as traders battened down for U.S. payroll data due later today. The All Ordinaries index added 6.20 points to 2,491.60, a rise of 16.90 from last Thursday.

JOHANNESBURG - South African shares ended strong boosted by bullish U.S. unemployment data which lifted industrials in the afternoon after a weaker start, golds ended at yet another fresh four-year low on a lacklustre bullion price which failed to break above the $340 an ounce level. The Industrial index ended up 44.2 points at 8,538.5, a rise of 132.5 from last Friday, the All-share index gained 18.5 points to 7,149.0, up 77 on the week and the Gold index lost 5.4 points to 1,181.6, down 53.4 from seven days ago.
